article.title: Ingesting events
article.lede: Events are the unit Meridian stores, indexes, and bills on. This page covers the two ways to get them in — the SDK for application code, and the HTTP endpoint for everything else.

sections.heading: Install the SDK
sections.body: The SDK batches events in memory and flushes on an interval, so a burst of calls costs one round trip. It is safe to call from request handlers.

sections.heading: Send your first event
sections.body: An event needs a name and a subject. Everything else is optional metadata that becomes queryable the moment it lands.

variants.label: TypeScript
Python
variants.code:
from meridian import Meridian

meridian = Meridian(api_key=os.environ["MERIDIAN_KEY"])

meridian.track(
    name="invoice.paid",
    subject="acct_18fj2",
    properties={"amount": 4900, "currency": "usd"},
)

sections.heading: Verify it landed
sections.body: The CLI tails the same stream the dashboard reads from, so you can confirm delivery without leaving the terminal.

params.name: name
params.description: Dot-separated event name. Used for grouping and billing.

params.name: subject
params.description: The entity the event is about — usually an account or user id.

params.name: properties
params.description: Arbitrary metadata. Keys become queryable within a minute of ingest.

nested.name: amount
nested.description: Minor units. Combined with currency for revenue rollups.

params.name: occurred_at
params.description: When the event happened. Defaults to receipt time; must fall inside the retention window.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.description: Repeat deliveries with the same key collapse to one stored event for 24 hours.

samples.label: TypeScript

releases.summary: Idempotency keys now hold for 24 hours instead of 1, and collapsed deliveries report `deduplicated: true` rather than failing silently.
Batches flush on process exit, so short-lived scripts no longer drop their last window.
`occurred_at` outside the retention window returns 422 with the window bounds instead of a generic validation error.
`events replay` gained `--dry-run`, which reports what would be re-emitted without emitting it.
The ingest endpoint moved from `/v2/track` to `/v3/events` and takes `subject` where v2 took `distinct_id`. v2 keeps accepting writes through 2027-01-01.
